chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Hassam, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said:

A slave of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) fell ill, so he (peace be upon him) asked about him, and it was said to him, 'He has a spleen ailment.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Feed him leeks for three days.' So we fed them to him, the blood settled, then he was cured.

key_terms.طُحَالٌ: Spleen ailment or disease of the spleen
key_terms.فَقَعَدَ الدَّمُ: The blood settled (stopped bleeding or congestion resolved)

ai.seo_question: What medical remedy did Imam al-Hassan (AS) prescribe for spleen illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Hassan (peace be upon him), demonstrating the integration of spiritual authority with empirical health practices in Shia tradition. The specific instruction to use leeks (*kurrath*) for three days to resolve blood stagnation (*da'm al-dam*) underscores the Prophetic tradition of utilizing natural remedies for physical ailments, reinforcing the holistic view of the Imams as healers of both body and soul.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr who said,

‘A slave of Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> complained, so he<sup>asws</sup> asked about him, and it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘He is with spleen illness’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Feed him the leek for three days’. So we fed it to him, so the blood settled, then he was cured’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Hassan from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “

Once, a slave of abu al-Hassan complained of illness. He (the Imam) asked about him and it was said that he has spleen trouble. He (the Imam) said, Teed him leeks for three days.’ We fed him, blood formed and he became well.’”
